newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil takes lead on U.S. cold weather report.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil takes lead on U.S. cold weather report.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures took the lead on Friday as forecasts of cold weather in key U.S. heating oil markets over the weekend boosted the product's price on both sides of the Atlantic, traders said.
May gas oil was trading $1 up at 163.25 a tonne by 1027 GMT having traded earlier at $163.50, while June Brent was 24 cents up at $24 a barrel.
Traders attributed gas oil's gains to cold weather forecasts for the U.S. Northeast and the Mideast.
Independent forecaster Weather Services Corp (WSC) said on Friday the cold weather would drive heating oil demand to well above normal over the next 48 hours.
"The prods are taking the lead," said one trader. "But we're also seeing a bit of a bounce after yesterday's losses.
Despite the gains the Brent remained fragile, and some speculated it would be prone to profit-taking ahead of the weekend.
"It just doesn't seem to be able to get above the $18 level," said one trader. "Everytime it tries to rally the market puts a lid on it."
Most traders said stabs at resistance around $18.50 level and the gap at $18.62-77 looked unlikely in Friday's session.
